title: Manage supply chain risk throughout acquisition and operation: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: What assurance evidence is proportionate for this supplier, component, update path, or hardware trust claim?
focalInsight: Assurance combines provenance, scoped assessment, enforceable terms, lifecycle monitoring, technical verification, and exit.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Puf
nodes.definition: Device-specific response from physical microstructure variation.
nodes.detail: Device-specific response from physical microstructure variation.
nodes.decision: Evaluate enrollment, helper data, reliability, side-channel, lifecycle.

nodes.label: Silicon Root Of Trust
nodes.decision: Check provisioning, update, interfaces, authority protection.
nodes.failureExample: Silicon label proves downstream trust claim.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Root establishes start, not entire chain.

nodes.label: Firmware Integrity
nodes.definition: Assurance firmware is authorized and unaltered.
nodes.detail: Assurance firmware is authorized and unaltered.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Assurance
nodes.definition: Evidence-backed confidence across procurement and operation.
nodes.detail: Evidence-backed confidence across procurement and operation.
nodes.decision: Combine provenance, terms, monitoring, response, exit.

altSummary: Assurance combines provenance, scoped assessment, enforceable terms, lifecycle monitoring, technical verification, and exit.
textFallback:
continuous monitoring: Ongoing supplier/component/change review. Decide: Set event, evidence, threshold, response. Example/failure: Ownership change never reassessed. Retrieve: Monitoring finds changed assurance.
puf: Device-specific response from physical microstructure variation. Decide: Evaluate enrollment, helper data, reliability, side-channel, lifecycle. Example/failure: PUF claim replaces key/update controls. Retrieve: PUF uniqueness is implementation-dependent.
silicon root of trust: Hardware/firmware foundation for initial verification. Decide: Check provisioning, update, interfaces, authority protection. Example/failure: Silicon label proves downstream trust claim. Retrieve: Root establishes start, not entire chain.
firmware integrity: Assurance firmware is authorized and unaltered. Decide: Protect signing/verification, update, rollback, recovery. Example/failure: PUF device accepts unsigned firmware. Retrieve: Identity does not authorize code.
supply chain assurance: Evidence-backed confidence across procurement and operation. Decide: Combine provenance, terms, monitoring, response, exit. Example/failure: Selection-day questionnaire is final assurance. Retrieve: Assurance continues through change.
